sections.h2: What does Brevard County look like to someone about to sell?
sections.html:
Brevard stretches along the central Florida east coast for 72 miles from north to south and holds roughly 600,000 residents. The county's own profile counts 16 municipalities and names two anchors that shape local demand, Kennedy Space Center and Patrick Space Force Base.

A seller in Titusville, Melbourne, Palm Bay or a small beachside city is therefore dealing with very different local governments under one county tax system. The county itself mainly serves people who live outside city limits, and the commission has five districts. The tax bill, though, runs on county rails wherever the house sits.

sections.h2: Which Brevard government handles permits, and which handles tax?
sections.html:
Permits depend on the address, while tax billing does not. For unincorporated land, county government issues building permits, reviews plans, enforces code, maintains local roads and bridges and supplies utilities. Inside a city, the city does most of that.

  • County services that reach everyone include 9-1-1 and emergency medical services, emergency management, mosquito control, libraries and parks.
  • Value comes from the appraiser's office, and the collector's office sends the bills and takes the money.
  • The county reports about 2,350 employees across 24 offices, none of which sets your assessed value.

The county's profile also lists a Valkaria Airport, a Natural Resources Management office and a Solid Waste Management office among its departments, a reminder that unincorporated owners deal with the county for services that city residents get from city hall.

Before a pre-sale repair, confirm which jurisdiction issues the permit. The mailing address on the tax bill can name a city that differs from the one that governs the lot.

sections.h2: What does the Brevard tax collector's year look like?
sections.html:
The collector publishes a calendar by month, and its discounts run on the postmark. Here are the entries a seller is likely to need.

sections.h2: Can a Brevard owner pay in quarterly installments?
sections.html:
Yes, when estimated tax is above $100. The collector's plan splits the year into four payments, due by June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, with the application, Form DR-534, due before May 1.

The June and September payments are figured from last year's gross tax. Changes from new value or exemptions are folded into the December and March payments after the roll is certified. Once enrolled and current, an owner does not reapply each year, as long as the first payment lands by June 30. If it has not arrived by July 31, participation is cancelled.

The collector warns that anyone with a mortgage escrow account should not use installments, because the lender pays in November to capture the largest discount. Questions go to (321) 264-6969, and the form goes to the collector at P.O. Box 2500, Titusville, FL 32781-2500. Any amount still unpaid on April 1 follows the normal delinquency rules.

sections.h2: What are the payment methods and fees in Brevard?
sections.html:
Standard bills are mailed by November 1, and the collector asks owners to call if nothing has arrived by the second week of November. Installment payers get bills quarterly, in June, September, December and March. A duplicate can be mailed on request.

  • E-checks made online are free, and a payment sent in error can be reversed by calling before 5:00 pm that day.
  • Credit and debit cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay carry a 2.75 percent fee with a $2.75 minimum. International cards are 3.95 percent. A third-party vendor keeps the fee.
  • A returned check draws a service charge under s. 68.065: $25 under $50, $30 from $50 to $299.99, $40 from $300 to $799.99, and 5 percent at $800 or more.
  • Wire payments must name the tax account number, the owner and the property ID, and cover all bank fees.

The collector adds that a current mailing address on file protects against ownership problems, which matters most for an owner who has already moved out.

sections.h2: What happens in Brevard when a bill is left unpaid?
sections.html:
In May, the late list for real estate is printed in a local paper on three consecutive weeks, and the ad cost plus an electronic fee land on the owner's balance. Certificates go up for sale as early as June 1 or soon after. Business property that is late gets one May listing, and warrants follow July 1.

A holder who has waited out the statutory period may then apply for a deed (s. 197.502). On a homestead, the opening bid includes half of the last assessed value, and a homestead balance under $250 is issued to the county, never auctioned.

sections.h2: Can the sale close while Brevard tax is unpaid?
sections.html:
Back taxes will not block a closing. The title agent still needs the collector's payoff and any certificate costs, so request them early. A sold certificate has to be redeemed at the table.

A deed to the buyer also resets the parcel to just value January 1, which ends the homestead growth limit, so the buyer's first bill can sit far above yours. Someone moving to another Florida house should ask about portability and Form DR-501T.

sections.h2: Who handles a value dispute or exemption question in Brevard?
sections.html:
Start with the Brevard County Property Appraiser, who answers at (321) 264-6700 per the collector's page. If the record misstates something simple, such as the bedroom count, a phone call may settle it. Formal petitions use the DR-486 forms, filed with the clerk inside 25 days of the August notice, or 30 days after an exemption denial letter.

Homestead applications are due March 1. The collector's home page has flagged Amendment 3, a homestead exemption ballot item, so check the appraiser's site for current exemption amounts before you quote a buyer next year's taxes.

sections.h2: What relief programs might an older or veteran Brevard owner ask about?
sections.html:
Several programs depend on local adoption, so ask the appraiser which apply in Brevard and your city.

  • Residents 65 and older: an ordinance may add as much as $50,000 for qualifying household income.
  • Disabled ex-servicemembers: a $5,000 assessed value reduction.
  • Veterans past 65 with a lasting service-related disability: a homestead discount tied to the VA percentage.
  • Homestead tax deferral: the collector lists March 31 as the filing deadline.

sections.h2: What do heirs in Brevard need to check before listing?
sections.html: Heirs lose the exemption once the owner is gone. Call the appraiser to learn how the transfer is treated, since certain transfers at death escape the ownership reset, and pull a payoff from the collector before the sign goes up.

faqs.q: Which Brevard office mails the tax notice?
faqs.a: The tax collector mails the November bill. The property appraiser mails the proposed tax notice in August.

faqs.q: What is the Brevard delinquency date?
faqs.a: April 1. Taxes unpaid then become delinquent, and certificates are offered on or before June 1.

faqs.q: What is the minimum for the Brevard installment plan?
faqs.a: Estimated tax must exceed $100, and the application on Form DR-534 must reach the collector before May 1.

faqs.q: Do mortgage escrow owners use installments in Brevard?
faqs.a: No. The collector says lenders pay in November to capture the discount, so installments are not for escrow accounts.

faqs.q: Is the Brevard discount based on postmark?
faqs.a: Yes, the collector's calendar says discounts are based on postmark, with 4 percent through November 30.
